takeaway: In the cardiac action potential sodium leaks INTO the cell, depolarizing it to threshold; calcium influx prolongs the plateau and potassium efflux repolarizes.

question.text: Regarding the cardiac action potential, which of the following statements is incorrect?

answer.text: Incorrect: there is a constant leak of sodium ions out of the cell.

lines.text: The wrong statement is the sodium leak going out of the cell.
In the pacemaker cell, sodium leaks constantly INTO the cell, like water into a leaky boat.
This slow leak raises the resting membrane potential until it reaches threshold.
Calcium ions then flood in and keep the wave high, which lengthens the cardiac action potential.
Finally, potassium flows out of the cell and repolarizes the membrane.
Acetylcholine slows the sodium leak, adrenaline speeds it up. But sodium never leaks out.
